title: U.S. Senate · New Mexico

context.text: Incumbent Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D), first elected in 2020, defeated Matt Dodson 84.2%-15.8% in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary. On the Republican side, Larry E. Marker ran as a write-in candidate in the primary (after a rival's signatures were rejected) and needed 2,351 write-in votes to qualify for the general-election ballot; he received 31,220 write-in votes and qualified. Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Decision Desk and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rated the general election Solid/Safe Democratic as of the primary.

candidates.name: Ben Ray Luján
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary 84.2%-15.8% over Matt Dodson.

summary.text: Ben Ray Luján is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Senator from New Mexico, first elected in 2020. He grew up in Nambé, worked in state government, served on the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (elected 2004), and represented New Mexico's 3rd Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2009 to 2021, including a term as House Assistant Speaker. He is seeking a second Senate term.

background.text: Born in Santa Fe, New Mexico, in 1972 and raised in Nambé; his father, Ben Luján, was a longtime member of the New Mexico House and its speaker. His Senate biography says he is a Head Start graduate.
Graduated from Pojoaque Valley High School in 1990 and earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from New Mexico Highlands University in 2007.
Worked as director of administrative services and chief financial officer of the New Mexico Cultural Affairs Department before entering elected office.

Elected to the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission in 2004, serving until the end of 2008 and as its chairman; his Senate biography says he worked with colleagues to develop a renewable portfolio standard.
Won the 3rd Congressional District seat in 2008 to succeed Tom Udall and served in the U.S. House from 2009 to 2021.

In the House he chaired the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, beginning with his selection by Nancy Pelosi in November 2014 as the first Latino to chair either party's campaign committee, and was elected assistant majority leader (Assistant Speaker) for the 116th Congress.

Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2020, defeating Republican Mark Ronchetti, and has served since January 2021; sits on the Commerce, Science, and Transportation; Finance; Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry; Indian Affairs; and Budget committees.
Suffered a serious stroke in 2022 that required hospitalization and surgery; he has since recovered and has advocated for stroke prevention and treatment efforts.

According to his Senate website, he received the James Beard Impact Award in June 2026 for work on the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and led efforts to strengthen the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act program.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Food and Nutrition, Specialty Crops, Organics, and Research); the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Telecommunications and Media); the Committee on Finance; the Committee on Indian Affairs; and the Committee on the Budget.

candidates.name: Larry E. Marker
candidates.ballotNote: Qualified for the general election as a write-in candidate in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 31,220 write-in votes.

summary.text: Larry E. Marker is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate from Roswell, New Mexico, and describes himself as a self-employed oil and gas businessman with experience in several industries. He ran for Commissioner of Public Lands in 2022 as an independent write-in and for the Republican nomination for State Senate District 27 in 2024, losing both, and qualified for the 2026 general election through a write-in primary campaign. His campaign website emphasizes oil and gas, border enforcement and relief from federal regulation of agriculture.

background.text: According to his campaign website, born in Hobbs in 1963 and raised in Roswell after his family settled there in 1972; he lists Roswell as his residence and is 62.

Per his campaign website, he has worked in oil and gas production, farming, ranching, manufacturing, construction and service; the Albuquerque Journal describes him as a self-employed oil and gas businessman.
The campaign website says he turned to grassroots conservative activism and study of the New Mexico Constitution and statutes after what it describes as years of confronting government overreach.

Ran for New Mexico Commissioner of Public Lands in 2022 as an independent write-in candidate, receiving 0.6% (3,950 votes) in the November general election won by incumbent Stephanie Garcia Richard (D).
Ran in the 2024 Republican primary for New Mexico State Senate District 27, finishing third with 15.4% behind Patrick Boone IV and incumbent Greg Nibert.
No Republican appeared on the June 2, 2026 U.S. Senate primary ballot; Marker qualified for the general election as a write-in candidate with 31,220 votes.

priorities.text: Energy: an "all-of-the-above" strategy to stop federal permitting restrictions, protect oil-and-gas-funded education spending, and make New Mexico a leader in oil, gas, hydrogen and nuclear development.
Border security: shutting down fentanyl trafficking, supporting Border Patrol and local law enforcement, and opposing policies he says shield violent offenders.
Agriculture: opposing what his campaign describes as regulatory overreach against farmers and ranchers, and defending grazing rights and water access.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for shutting down fentanyl trafficking routes and increased support for Border Patrol and local law enforcement at the border.
